Semester 3: Adult Health Nursing Begins

Read the summary line. If it feels unfamiliar, open the chapter and study the diagram.

Adult Health Nursing I

Introduction & Perioperative Care

  • Perioperative nursing — preoperative assessment, preparation, intraoperative care and postoperative recovery.
  • Describe preoperative assessment and preparation
  • Explain intraoperative nursing care

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Introduction to Microbiology

  • What microbiology is, types of microbes, and why microbiology matters in nursing and infection prevention.
  • Define microbiology and name the types of microbes
  • Explain why microbiology matters in nursing

Pathology I

General Pathology

  • General pathology — cell injury, inflammation, healing and repair.
  • Define pathology and its branches
  • Describe cell injury, necrosis and apoptosis

Pharmacology I

General Pharmacology

  • Pharmacology basics — drug sources, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and routes of administration.
  • Define pharmacology and its branches
  • Describe pharmacokinetics (ADME) and pharmacodynamics

Adult Health Nursing I

Intraoperative Care

  • Intraoperative nursing — scrub and circulating roles, sterile technique, patient positioning, anaesthesia basics.
  • Describe scrub and circulating nurse roles
  • Explain sterile technique and surgical counts

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

General Characteristics of Microbes

  • Structure of bacteria and viruses, Gram staining, bacterial growth and spore formation.
  • Describe the structure of a bacterial cell
  • Explain Gram staining and its significance

Pathology I

Systemic Pathology

  • Systemic pathology — common diseases of major body systems (heart, lung, liver, kidney).
  • Describe common pathologies of heart, lung, liver and kidney
  • Explain atherosclerosis, pneumonia, cirrhosis and nephritis

Pharmacology I

Antiseptics & Disinfectants

  • Antiseptics and disinfectants — differences, common agents, uses and safety.
  • Differentiate antiseptics from disinfectants
  • Name common antiseptics and disinfectants and their uses

Adult Health Nursing I

Common Signs & Symptoms: Shock, Pain, Fluids

  • Common signs and symptoms — shock, pain, fluid imbalance — recognition and nursing care.
  • Describe types and signs of shock
  • Assess and manage pain

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Pathogenic Organisms

  • Common disease-causing bacteria, viruses and fungi and the infections they cause.
  • Name common pathogenic bacteria and their diseases
  • Name common pathogenic viruses and their diseases

Pathology I

Haematological Tests & Blood Bank

  • Haematological tests — CBC, bleeding/clotting times, blood grouping, cross-matching and transfusion.
  • List haematological tests and their purposes
  • Describe blood grouping and cross-matching

Pharmacology I

Drugs Acting on the GI System

  • GI drugs — antacids, antiemetics, laxatives, antidiarrhoeals and their uses.
  • List GI drug classes and examples
  • Describe uses of antacids, antiemetics, laxatives and antidiarrhoeals

Adult Health Nursing I

Respiratory Disorders

  • Respiratory disorders — COPD, asthma, pneumonia, tuberculosis — assessment and nursing care.
  • Describe COPD, asthma, pneumonia and tuberculosis
  • State nursing care for respiratory patients

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Immunity & Immunization

  • Types of immunity, how vaccines work, and the national immunisation schedule.
  • Define innate and acquired immunity
  • Describe active and passive immunity

Pharmacology I

Drugs Acting on the Respiratory System

  • Respiratory drugs — bronchodilators, antihistamines, decongestants, expectorants and antitussives.
  • List respiratory drug classes and examples
  • Describe bronchodilators, antihistamines, decongestants, expectorants

Adult Health Nursing I

Digestive Disorders

  • Digestive disorders — peptic ulcer, gastritis, hepatitis, cirrhosis, cholecystitis, pancreatitis — nursing care.
  • Describe common digestive disorders
  • Explain nursing care for GI patients

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Hospital-Acquired Infections

  • What HAIs are, common types, risk factors and how to prevent them.
  • Define hospital-acquired infection
  • List common types of HAIs

Pharmacology I

Cardiovascular & Blood Drugs

  • Cardiovascular drugs — antihypertensives, antianginals, antiarrhythmics, diuretics, anticoagulants, antiplatelets.
  • List cardiovascular drug classes and examples
  • Describe uses of antihypertensives, antianginals, anticoagulants

Adult Health Nursing I

Cardiovascular Disorders

  • Cardiovascular disorders — hypertension, angina, MI, heart failure, arrhythmias — nursing care.
  • Describe hypertension, angina, MI, heart failure and arrhythmias
  • Explain nursing care for cardiac patients

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Isolation Precautions & PPE

  • Isolation precautions, types of transmission-based precautions and correct PPE use.
  • Describe standard and transmission-based precautions
  • List contact, droplet and airborne precautions

Pharmacology I

Endocrine Drugs

  • Endocrine drugs — insulin, oral hypoglycaemics, thyroid drugs, corticosteroids.
  • List endocrine drug classes and examples
  • Describe insulin types and administration

Adult Health Nursing I

Blood Disorders

  • Blood disorders — anaemia, leukaemia, clotting disorders, thrombocytopenia — nursing care.
  • Describe anaemia, leukaemia and clotting disorders
  • Explain nursing care for blood disorder patients

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Hand Hygiene

  • Hand hygiene — when to do it, soap vs alcohol rub, correct technique and the WHO 5 moments.
  • State the WHO 5 moments of hand hygiene
  • Describe correct handwashing and hand-rub technique

Pharmacology I

Integumentary Drugs

  • Skin drugs — topical corticosteroids, antifungals, antiseptics, emollients and keratolytics.
  • List skin drug classes and examples
  • Describe uses of topical corticosteroids, antifungals and antiseptics

Adult Health Nursing I

Endocrine Disorders

  • Endocrine disorders — diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Cushing's, Addison's — nursing care.
  • Describe diabetes mellitus types and management
  • Explain hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Disinfection & Sterilisation

  • Disinfection vs sterilisation, methods, levels of disinfection and sterilising equipment.
  • Differentiate disinfection from sterilisation
  • Name methods of disinfection and sterilisation

Pharmacology I

Antimicrobial & Antitubercular Drugs

  • Antimicrobials — penicillins, cephalosporins, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides and antitubercular drugs.
  • List antimicrobial classes and examples
  • Describe antitubercular drugs and their regimen

Adult Health Nursing I

Integumentary Disorders

  • Skin disorders — dermatitis, eczema, psoriasis, pressure ulcers, skin infections, burns — nursing care.
  • Describe common skin disorders
  • Explain pressure ulcer prevention and staging

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Specimen Collection

  • Collecting blood, urine, sputum, stool and wound swabs correctly for culture and testing.
  • Describe correct collection of blood, urine, sputum, stool and wound swabs
  • State how to prevent contamination

Adult Health Nursing I

Musculoskeletal Disorders

  • Musculoskeletal disorders — fractures, arthritis, osteoporosis, osteomyelitis, amputations — nursing care.
  • Describe common musculoskeletal disorders
  • Explain fracture care and immobilisation

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Biomedical Waste Management

  • Biomedical waste categories, colour-coded segregation, safe handling and disposal.
  • List biomedical waste categories and colour coding
  • Describe safe segregation and handling

Adult Health Nursing I

Communicable Diseases

  • Communicable diseases — TB, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, typhoid, malaria — transmission, prevention, nursing care.
  • Describe common communicable diseases and transmission
  • Explain isolation precautions and infection control

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Antibiotic Stewardship & AMR

  • Antibiotic resistance, why it happens, and how nurses support stewardship.
  • Define antimicrobial resistance and how it develops
  • Describe how nurses support antibiotic stewardship

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Patient Safety Indicators

  • Patient safety indicators — what they are, common indicators and how nurses improve them.
  • Define patient safety indicators
  • List common patient safety indicators

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

International Patient Safety Goals

  • IPSG — the six goals: identify patients, improve communication, improve medication safety, ensure correct surgery, reduce infection, reduce falls.
  • List the six International Patient Safety Goals
  • Describe what each goal means in practice

Applied Microbiology & Infection Control

Safety Protocols & Emergency Codes

  • Hospital safety protocols and emergency codes — fire, cardiac arrest, infant abduction, violence, evacuation.
  • List common emergency codes and their meanings
  • Describe fire safety (RACE, PASS)
